title: You Drive Through a Toll at Highway Speed and Never Stop
fb_caption: No booth, no braking, and the toll still gets paid. The little tag on your windshield is a radio ID. As you pass, a reader on the overhead gantry pings it, the tag answers with its ID, and the toll is matched to your account and charged automatically. Many sticker tags don't even have a battery: the reader's radio signal powers them for that instant. No tag? Cameras snap your license plate and the bill comes by mail. Tag on the windshield or bill by mail: which are you?
engagement_comment: Tag on the windshield or bill by mail: which are you? 1 = tag, always, 2 = bill by mail, 3 = I avoid toll roads.
sources: Wikipedia, E-ZPass (RFID transponder read at lane-based or open-road toll points; prepaid account debited; vehicles without a transponder are photographed by plate and the owner billed): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-ZPass
Wikipedia, SunPass (SunPass Mini: passive RFID sticker transponder, uses no batteries): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SunPass
Wikipedia, Radio-frequency identification (passive tags are powered by energy from the reader's interrogating radio waves): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio-frequency_identification

tts.director_notes: Calm, curious American male explainer, warm and clear, brisk pace, short pause before the twist.

beats.text: You drive under a toll at highway speed, never stop, and still pay.
That little tag on your windshield is a radio ID, like a tiny name badge for your car.
As you pass, a reader on the overhead gantry pings it, and the tag answers with its ID.
The toll is matched to your account and charged automatically.
Here's the twist. Many sticker tags have no battery. The reader's radio signal powers them for that instant.
No tag? Cameras snap your license plate, and the bill comes by mail.
Tag on the windshield or bill by mail: which are you? Tell us below.
